title: A glossary pop-up isn't teaching
statement: Don't count a glossary pop-up as teaching a word.
detail: A grade-3 reading rulebook's vocabulary routine says never to target a word the passage explains in place and that a glossary pop-up is never instruction, beside rules to prefer generative words and never to assess a word the turn it was taught. The same routine asks for about 12 productions of each target word per lesson, where a recognition click is not a production. The rulebook says it is grounded in BrainLifts on direct instruction, practice and knowledge, a reading-science corpus and five rounds of rulings from review.
against: A content audit of the same course counts a glossary as introducing a word: "The **video transcript counts as delivered instruction** — anything the narration says is introduced, on equal footing with a vocab card or glossary." (`shadow-content-eval/SKILL.md`, line 63), cited on the record teach-a-word-before-using-it. That check asks whether a word was introduced before it was used, not whether it was taught.

evidence.quote: Open frames end in BECAUSE / SO THAT; contrast near-neighbours; never assess a word the turn you taught it; a glossary pop-up is never instruction; prefer generative words; never target a word the passage explains in place.
~12 productions per target word per lesson (a recognition click is not a production; speaking counts and beats writing).
BrainLifts (Direct Instruction, Practice, Curriculum & Knowledge), the reading-science corpus
